_comment: Hosts and paths the blocker must never neutralise.
The plugin loads nothing from any of them. They are the opposite:
payment gateways and fraud checks a site's own shop and forms rely on.
Both are exempt from consent under ePrivacy — a payment is the service
the buyer asked for, and a fraud check protects them — and blocking
either protects nobody: a neutralised payment script takes the card
fields off the checkout page, so the shop stops taking money from every
visitor who has not accepted marketing.
In a data file rather than as PHP literals for the same reason as
technical-hosts.json: written in code, a list of host names reads to an
analyser as the plugin offloading its own assets, which is a different
thing and is not allowed in the directory.
Unlike the technical hosts, this list is NOT a setting. An editable list
is one somebody can empty by accident, and a checkout that breaks
because of a tidy-up in a settings screen is not a good trade. Sites
with a gateway that is not here use the
_paths_comment: Matched anywhere in the address, whatever the host. reCAPTCHA is served
from www.google.com and www.gstatic.com, the same hosts as Google Maps,
so the host alone cannot tell them apart: with those categorised as
marketing, the CAPTCHA on every contact form went down with the maps.
